newsitem.title: USA: Coffee at 20-year high; Starbucks hikes prices again.
newsitem.headline: Coffee at 20-year high; Starbucks hikes prices again.

text.p: The price of coffee leaped to a 20-year high on the free-wheeling futures market Wednesday, prompting upscale coffee retailer Starbucks Corp. to raise prices again.
On New York's Coffee Sugar and Cocoa Exchange, coffee for July delivery rose 12.70 cents to $2.87 per pound, the highest in two decades.
The sizzling rise has been fuelled by jitters about cold weather in Brazil at a time when coffee inventories are already low and supply is tight from Latin America.

Roasters have been passing on to consumers the higher cost of buying coffee. On Wednesday, Starbucks' store managers said the company plans to raise prices by five cents a cup, bringing the cost of a tall coffee in some retail outlets to $1.25. Whole bean prices are also expected to rise.
The increase is the second time Seattle-based Starbucks has raised prices this year. In March, it added five cents to the price of a cup and bean prices went up 30 cents a pound.
A spokesman for Starbucks was not immediately available for comment.
Last week, Maxwell House Coffee Co., a unit of Philip Morris' Kraft Foods, and Procter & Gamble Co.'s Folger Coffee Co. also boosted their prices.

Forecasts for cool winter weather in Brazil, the biggest exporter, did not point to a damaging frost. But they were enough to trigger new speculative buying in a rally that has lifted prices for American arabica coffees by 150 percent since the beginning of the year.

"Coffee is physically tight with stockpiles in both consumer and producer countries at 20-year lows, and this makes the market extremely prone to weather scares in Brazil," said the brokerage house GNI Ltd.

According to the latest weather reports, cooler-than-normal conditions are expected in the coffee belt this week. However, no damaging cold is indicated, as there are no major cold airmasses forecast to build out of Argentina.
